title: stage_3_2_marathon_voice
full_text: In 1904, an Olympic runner won gold using rat poison and brandy. The St. Louis marathon was a ninety-degree nightmare with only one water station across twenty-six dust-choked miles. Only fourteen of thirty-two competitors finished alive. One runner was chased a mile off course into a cornfield by aggressive stray dogs. Meanwhile, a Cuban postman ran in street boots, stopped to eat apples, took an hour nap, and finished fourth! When leader Thomas Hicks began collapsing, his handlers administered doses of strychnine rat poison mixed with brandy. Hallucinating wildly and barely conscious, Hicks was carried across the finish line to claim Olympic gold. It remains the most chaotic race in athletic history.
